Cc: ops@mercuryai.com
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: High p99 latency + spike in 500s this morning (MercuryAI)

Hi Aditya,

We started seeing a sharp increase in user-facing p99 latency and a burst of 500s starting ~08:40 PT this morning. Affected endpoints are our /chat/generate route (model: rwd-13b-q4) and a downstream ranking step that calls Redwood embeddings. Key metrics:
- p50 ~ 120ms -> unchanged
- p99 jumped from ~420ms to ~2.8s between 08:40–09:10 PT
- Error rate (5xx) spiked to 4.2% for the 30m window (baseline ~0.1%)

We attached a brief sample of request IDs and a tail of logs with headers (mercuryai_error_sample.log). The customer impact was live traffic degraded for ~30 minutes; we rerouted a small % of traffic while investigating. Can you confirm whether this looks like a runtime or cache configuration issue on your side? Anything we can toggle quickly?

This is blocking an external demo at 10:30 PT — we need an ETA for mitigation and a clear rollback if required.

Thanks,
Alyssa
Alyssa Green

Quick notes:
- I’ve looped in Marissa (SRE lead) and Jonas (runtime) to investigate KV cache behavior and routing.

Immediate plan:
1) We’ll snapshot current KV occupancy and the active priority-lane map (Jonas).
2) If we see HOL blocking, we’ll temporarily disable aggressive prefix pinning for Mercury and enable the emergency prefetch-throttle to reduce thrash.
3) I’ll coordinate a 30-minute hotfix window and share a customer-facing note.

Can you keep the logs rolling to the same bucket and share any additional request IDs if you see reoccurrence?

— Aditya

Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 10:01:05 -0700
Subject: RE: High p99 latency + spike in 500s this morning (MercuryAI) — initial findings

We pulled diagnostics and KV snapshot attached (kv_snapshot_20260617.json). Early signs:
- Several shards show sustained high occupancy from a small prefix set (Mercury has multiple long prefixes pinned since last config roll).
- We observed priority-lane head-of-line blocking where large batched requests are monopolizing KV workers and preventing prefetch progress for regular-low latency lanes.
- There are also elevated eviction rates coincident with an autoscaling event at 08:36 PT — that created transient pointer-churn while the prefetch window was expanding.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (ordered):
1) Rollback recent prefix pinning changes for Mercury (last change: 2026-06-15 policy update).
2) Turn on prefetch-throttle for the affected machines (cap concurrent prefetch jobs to 12).
3) Temporarily lower batch size for Mercury routes to avoid HOL monopolization.
4) Increase KV eviction grace to 45s to avoid cascading evictions during autoscale.

I’ll run the rollback + prefetch throttle now if we have exec sign-off. If the rollback is risky, alternative is to spin a temporary dedicated lane for Mercury traffic (30m to provision).

Attaching a short playbook with step-by-step commands (playbook_hotfix_v1.pdf).

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Action plan: immediate rollback and throttles (ETA 20–30m)

Hi Alyssa — quick update and what we’re doing now so you can share with your PMs/demo team:

What went wrong (short):
- A recent prefix-pinning policy plus concurrent autoscale triggered KV eviction churn and head-of-line blocking. That caused spikes in p99 and a short burst of 5xx as prefetches timed out.

What we’re doing (now):
- Rolling back the 2026-06-15 prefix pinning for Mercury.
- Enabling prefetch-throttle (concurrent prefetch jobs capped) to reduce thrash.
- Reducing batch size for Mercury routes to lower HOL contention.

Timing: rollback + throttle takes ~10–20 minutes; we’ll verify metrics for a 15-minute window and keep you updated. If we don’t see improvement, we’ll provision a dedicated lane and switch your traffic (estimated +30m).

Attachments: playbook_hotfix_v1.pdf (commands we’re executing).

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll follow up with a short post-mortem including root cause and longer-term mitigations (prefetch safeguards + config gating).

— Aditya
